messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: quick print
parts:
Hi, this has come up before . . . sometimes I fit a Stan program with some high-dimensional parameters, so print() won't do the job. And it can be a pain in the ass to fire up Shinystan. I'd like a print() which does a quick summary, one line showing max(R-hat) for each named parameter, maybe some other stuff too, just something quick to see mixing.
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] quick print
parts:
We have a GitHub issue tracker for RStan.

The more precise the request, the easier it is to fulfill.

Not sure what you want because print(fit) can only have one
behavior. Do you want a different function name?

I know you've wanted to trim down what print() does. I'm
pretty sure you're in the minority on that one, but if you
come up with a spec for what you do want, we can write another
function for you.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] quick print
parts:
Isn’t Rhat computed using the same intermediate calculations as ESS?
In other words, I’m pretty sure that dropping from 10 output columns
to 1 won’t result in anything close to a factor of 10 improvement in speed.
